blindSummary:
In this country same-sex conduct is criminalised (up to death under some interpretations of the penal code; 100 lashes/1 year otherwise), but a rights review emphasises the operative mechanism: the erosion of the rule of law and the power of armed groups has facilitated a surge in attacks targeting transgender individuals — de facto criminalisation operating outside any judicial system. Areas under an armed religious movement's control impose their own moral-policing regime; other regions fall under their own militia authorities.

For a visitor: no safe authority to appeal to anywhere in the country.
blindOutOfScope: War risk affects all; the documented surge in trans-targeted attacks is trans-specific.
blindSourceSummaries: Rights-group country review: the erosion of the rule of law, the humanitarian crisis and militia influence have facilitated a surge in attacks on trans people; criminalisation operates through less formal channels - non-state actors and civilians acting outside the judicial system, with morality laws serving as justification for vigilante action; legal provisions apply only in government-controlled areas amid the ongoing conflict.

International human-rights organisation report (April 2018) on LGBT activism across several countries of the region - includes this country's criminalisation and an annex of the laws used to punish same-sex conduct and gender expression across that region.

The same organisation's 2026 annual review of the global picture, chapter on this country: it remains one of the world's worst humanitarian crises (19.5 million needing assistance); includes a sexual-orientation and gender-identity section documenting abuses amid the conflict and armed-group control.

Another international human-rights organisation (Feb 2024): the armed movement must stop executions and release dozens facing LGBTI charges - courts it operates sentenced 40+ people to death, flogging or prison across two cities: in one, nine were sentenced to death (seven by stoning, two by crucifixion) and 23 to prison for 'homosexuality' and 'spreading immorality'; in the other, 13 students were sentenced to death for 'spreading homosexuality' - the sentences were described as gruesome public spectacles aimed at spreading fear.

Legal-aid site statute page: under a 1994 penal code, unmarried men face 100 lashes or up to 1 year for male homosexuality, married men death by stoning; female homosexuality carries up to 3 years, or up to 7 years under duress.

Wire-service feature (Aug 2013) by a correspondent, portraying a country with no place for gay people: a 19-year-old who spent his childhood under semi-house arrest tucks his long hair inside a hood to pass checkpoints in the capital - a portrait of daily concealment and fear.
blindTangential: Same-sex conduct criminalised (up to death under some interpretations; 100 lashes/1 year otherwise) — a catastrophic exposure for trans visitors with partners or perceived as same-sex-active.
